questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é uma paisagem natural?
options: Uma paisagem só com ruas e carros
Uma paisagem quase sem mudanças feitas pelas pessoas
questions.answer: Uma paisagem quase sem mudanças feitas pelas pessoas
questions.hint: Pense no que existe antes de as pessoas construírem.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes lugares é um exemplo de paisagem natural?
questions.hint: Qual lugar não foi construído pelas pessoas?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes elementos da paisagem foi feito pelas pessoas?
questions.hint: Três deles a natureza fez sozinha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama a paisagem que foi transformada pelo trabalho das pessoas? Paisagem ___.
questions.hint: É o contrário de paisagem natural.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma praia com quiosques, calçadão e prédios na beira do mar é uma paisagem…
questions.hint: Veja se há coisas construídas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Numa foto antiga de um bairro há chácaras e muitas árvores. Na foto atual há prédios e ruas asfaltadas. O que aconteceu com a paisagem?
questions.hint: Compare o que existia antes com o que existe agora.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas transformações acontece pela própria natureza, sem as pessoas?
options: Uma rocha se desgastar com a chuva e o vento
questions.answer: Uma rocha se desgastar com a chuva e o vento
questions.hint: Três delas precisam do trabalho humano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual rio de São Paulo teve seu caminho alterado e hoje tem grandes avenidas nas margens, as Marginais?
questions.hint: É um rio que atravessa a cidade de São Paulo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Antigamente, a Avenida Paulista tinha grandes casarões. O que existe hoje em grande parte dela?
options: Prédios altos de escritórios e lojas
questions.answer: Prédios altos de escritórios e lojas
questions.hint: Pense em como é uma avenida movimentada no centro de uma cidade grande.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que meio de transporte circulava pelos trilhos das ruas de São Paulo antigamente e não circula mais hoje?
questions.hint: Ele andava sobre trilhos no meio da rua, puxado por energia elétrica.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que as pessoas modificam as paisagens?
options: Para mudar a cor do céu
Para construir casas, ruas e plantações
questions.answer: Para construir casas, ruas e plantações
questions.hint: Pense nas necessidades das pessoas que moram num lugar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Ao comparar uma foto antiga e uma foto atual do mesmo lugar, observamos as permanências e as ___.
questions.hint: É o que ficou diferente de uma foto para a outra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma área de mata foi derrubada para construir um bairro. O que pode acontecer?
options: Os animais perdem o lugar onde viviam
questions.answer: Os animais perdem o lugar onde viviam
questions.hint: Pense em quem morava na mata.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Um parque com lago artificial, caminhos de pedra e árvores plantadas é uma paisagem…
questions.hint: O lago e os caminhos foram feitos por quem?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Pense na rua da sua casa ou da sua escola. Cite dois elementos naturais e dois elementos feitos pelas pessoas.
questions.hint: Árvores e céu são naturais; e o que foi construído?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Você acha importante preservar algumas paisagens naturais? Explique por quê.
questions.hint: Pense nos animais, nas plantas e nas pessoas.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of an explanation text?
options: To give instructions for a recipe
To explain how or why something happens
To persuade you to buy something
questions.answer: To explain how or why something happens
questions.hint: Think about the word 'explain'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best title for an explanation text?
questions.hint: Explanation titles often ask how or why.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explanation texts about natural processes are usually written in which tense?
questions.hint: The process still happens today, again and again.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which conjunction shows cause and effect?
questions.hint: Which word tells you the reason something happens?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the best causal conjunction: The puddle dries up ___ the sun heats the water.
questions.hint: The sun's heat is the reason the puddle dries.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In the water cycle, what is it called when liquid water turns into water vapour?
questions.hint: It happens when the sun warms the sea.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the technical word for rain, snow, sleet or hail falling from clouds?
questions.hint: It is one of the main stages of the water cycle and starts with 'p'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When water vapour cools and turns back into tiny droplets that form clouds, this is called…
questions.hint: Think of the droplets on a cold window.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Water has collected in the sea. Which stage of the water cycle comes next?
questions.hint: The water must rise into the air first.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a time connective to show the order of a process?
options: Next, the water vapour rises into the sky.
questions.answer: Next, the water vapour rises into the sky.
questions.hint: Look for a word that tells you when.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature would you NOT normally find in an explanation text?
options: A title that asks a question
questions.hint: Explanation texts are non-fiction.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a glossary?
options: A list of technical words and their meanings
questions.answer: A list of technical words and their meanings
questions.hint: It helps readers understand difficult words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which ending shows the effect? 'When the temperature drops below zero, ___'
questions.hint: What happens to water when it gets very cold?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which technical word names the hard case a caterpillar forms before it becomes a butterfly?
questions.hint: It starts with 'ch'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence would make the best final paragraph of an explanation about rain?
options: This is how water keeps moving around our planet, again and again.
Once upon a time there was a lonely cloud.
questions.answer: This is how water keeps moving around our planet, again and again.
questions.hint: A good ending sums up the process.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write two sentences explaining what happens to a puddle on a hot day. Use 'because' or 'so'.
questions.hint: Think about what the sun does to the water.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a journal?
options: A diary where someone writes what happens each day
questions.answer: A diary where someone writes what happens each day
questions.hint: Explorers write in one every evening.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a biography?
options: A true account of a person's life written by someone else
A story a person writes about their own life
questions.answer: A true account of a person's life written by someone else
questions.hint: 'Bio' means life.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Journals are usually written in which person?
questions.hint: The writer is telling about their own day.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read this journal entry: '3rd March 1852. We left the port of Kelmouth at dawn. The sea was calm.' On what date did the journey begin?
questions.hint: Look at the start of the entry.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: '10th April. After five weeks at sea, we finally saw land — a green island with tall cliffs.' What did the explorer see on 10th April?
options: A green island with tall cliffs
questions.answer: A green island with tall cliffs
questions.hint: Find the words after 'we finally saw land'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Born in 1820 in a small fishing village, Ada Thorne dreamed of the frozen north.' Where was Ada Thorne born?
questions.hint: Look for the place in the sentence.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Tomas Rell was born in 1790. He reached the great mountain pass in 1823.' How old was he when he reached the pass?
questions.hint: Subtract the year he was born from the year he reached the pass.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'In 1838, Ada joined a whaling ship as a cook. In 1848, she led her own expedition. In 1845, she learnt to navigate by the stars.' Which event happened second?
options: She learnt to navigate by the stars
She joined a whaling ship as a cook
questions.answer: She learnt to navigate by the stars
questions.hint: Put the years in order from earliest to latest.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word in this sentence signals time? 'Eventually, he returned home.'
questions.hint: Which word tells you when?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Day 12. Snow again. Our food is running low and the dogs are tired.' How do you think the explorer feels?
questions.hint: Think about having little food in the snow.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'We crossed the River Senna on 2nd June and reached the village of Orlo two days later.' On what date did they reach Orlo?
questions.hint: Count two days on from 2nd June.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do explorers keep journals?
options: To tell jokes to the crew
To record what they see and do each day
questions.answer: To record what they see and do each day
questions.hint: Think about remembering a long journey.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is most likely from a biography, not a journal?
options: She was born in a cold northern town in 1801.
Today I saw a whale beside our ship!
questions.answer: She was born in a cold northern town in 1801.
questions.hint: A biography uses 'he' or 'she'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is chronological order?
options: The order in which events happened
questions.answer: The order in which events happened
questions.hint: 'Chrono' is about time.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Before setting off, Mira Kade spent a year studying maps. During the voyage she discovered a hidden bay. After returning home, she wrote a book.' What did Mira do after returning home?
questions.hint: Find the words 'after returning home'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Would you rather read an explorer's journal or a biography about them? Give one reason.
questions.hint: Think about whose voice you would hear.

en_spell.topic: Year 3/4 statutory words: quarter to straight

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: qu_rt_r (one of four equal parts)
questions.hint: It sounds like 'kwor-ter' but the first vowel after 'qu' is an 'a'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: qu_st_on (something you ask)
questions.hint: Think 'quest' + 'ion'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling is correct?
questions.hint: Say it slowly: re-mem-ber.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: sp_c_al (very important or different)
questions.hint: The 'sh' sound in the middle is spelled with 'ci'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: str_ _ght (not bent or curved)
questions.hint: The long 'ay' sound here is spelled with four letters: a-i-g-h.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'a period when a king or queen rules'?
questions.hint: This homophone has a silent 'g'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: r_c_nt (happened not long ago)
questions.hint: The 's' sound is made by a letter 'c' followed by 'e'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: reg_l_r (happening at the same times, again and again)
questions.hint: Think of the word 'regulate'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the tricky part of the word 'quarter'?
questions.hint: Say the word and listen to the vowel after 'qu'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Complete the sentence: Please write a full ___ with a capital letter and a full stop.
questions.hint: It is a group of words that makes complete sense.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Unscramble the letters to make a word from your list: T H I G R A S T
questions.hint: It starts with 'str'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which sentence uses 'reign' correctly?
options: The queen's reign lasted fifty years.
We stayed inside because of the reign.
questions.answer: The queen's reign lasted fifty years.
questions.hint: Which one is about a ruler?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: speshal → special; remeber → remember; sentance → sentence; seperate → separate; quater → quarter
questions.text: Our teacher asked a speshal question about the recent storm. I had to remeber what happened and write one sentance about it. Then we had to seperate our answers into two groups: things we saw and things we heard. My group finished in a quater of an hour.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling means 'to split into groups'?
questions.hint: There is 'a rat' hiding in the middle of this word.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word for 'a group of words that makes complete sense'?
questions.hint: Both vowels after the 't' and 'n' are the same letter.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words in this swimming story.
questions.answer: reguler → regular; qestion → question; strait → straight; resent → recent; remmember → remember
questions.text: Every Saturday, Tomas goes to his reguler swimming lesson. His coach always asks the same qestion: can you swim in a strait line? Last week, in a resent race, Tomas tried his best. He will always remmember the moment he touched the wall first and his whole family cheered.

ipc.topic: Explorers and Adventurers: why do people explore?

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is an explorer?
options: A person who travels to discover new places
A person who only stays at home
questions.answer: A person who travels to discover new places
questions.hint: Think about the word 'explore'.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which of these is a reason people explored in the past?
options: To find new places to trade goods
questions.answer: To find new places to trade goods
questions.hint: Long ago, people wanted spices, silk and gold.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What word means 'buying, selling or swapping goods'?
questions.hint: Merchants did this at markets and ports.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What word means 'a strong wish to know or learn something'?
questions.hint: It comes from the word 'curious'.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which quality helps an explorer keep going when a journey gets hard?
questions.hint: It means not giving up.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which tool did sailors long ago use to find which direction was north?
questions.hint: Its needle is magnetic.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Some explorers wanted fame. What does 'fame' mean?
options: Being known by lots of people
questions.answer: Being known by lots of people
questions.hint: Famous people have it.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which of these was a big danger for sailors on very long sea voyages long ago?
options: running out of fresh food and water
getting lost in a shopping centre
questions.answer: running out of fresh food and water
questions.hint: They could be at sea for months.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What do we call the record an explorer writes each day about their journey? (one word)
questions.hint: It is a kind of daily notebook.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why do modern explorers go to the deep ocean or to space?
options: To learn new things through science
questions.answer: To learn new things through science
questions.hint: Today, a lot of exploring is about research.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which continent is covered in ice and was one of the last to be explored?
questions.hint: It is at the South Pole.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which quality means being ready to face danger even when you feel scared?
questions.hint: Brave people show it.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why did explorers need maps?
options: To plan routes and record where they had been
questions.answer: To plan routes and record where they had been
questions.hint: Maps show places and directions.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a good quality for an explorer?
questions.hint: Look for the one that would stop a journey.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Choose one reason why people explore (trade, curiosity or fame). Explain why it might make someone go on a dangerous journey.
questions.hint: Think about what the explorer hoped to gain.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: If you were an explorer, which place would you most like to discover, and which quality would help you most? Explain.
questions.hint: Name a place and one quality, then give a reason.

questions.subject: math
questions.hint: Share the tens first, then the ones.

questions.subject: math
questions.hint: How many 3s in 6 tens? How many 3s in 9 ones?

questions.subject: math
questions.hint: Think of your 7 times table.

questions.subject: math
questions.hint: Divide 9 tens by 6 and carry the remainder to the ones.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use short division: 368 ÷ 4 = ?
questions.hint: 4 does not go into 3, so start with 36 tens.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use short division: 525 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.hint: Watch out for the zero in the tens place.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use short division: 744 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.hint: Carry the remainder to the next column each time.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use short division: 952 ÷ 8 = ?
questions.hint: Start with 9 hundreds ÷ 8.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is 47 ÷ 5? Give your answer as a number with a remainder, like '9 r 2'.
questions.hint: How many 5s fit into 47? What is left over?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is 158 ÷ 6? Write it like '26 r 2'.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: In 72 ÷ 8 = 9, which number is the divisor?
questions.hint: It is the number you divide by.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: In 72 ÷ 8 = 9, which number is the quotient?
questions.hint: It is the answer to a division.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A baker puts 6 cakes in each box. She has 75 cakes. How many boxes can she fill completely?
questions.hint: Work out 75 ÷ 6 and think about what to do with the remainder.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: 30 children need to travel in cars. Each car takes 4 children. How many cars are needed so everyone can go?
questions.hint: 30 ÷ 4 has a remainder. Can any child be left behind?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Sweets are shared equally between 7 friends. There are 100 sweets. How many sweets are left over?
questions.hint: Find 100 ÷ 7 and look at the remainder.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Lia says 85 ÷ 4 = 21 r 1. Is she correct? Explain how you could check her answer using multiplication.
questions.hint: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: O que é um parágrafo?
options: Um trecho do texto que reúne uma ideia principal
questions.answer: Um trecho do texto que reúne uma ideia principal
questions.hint: Pense em como o texto é dividido em blocos.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Como começa cada parágrafo?
options: Com um pequeno espaço da margem e letra maiúscula
Com letra minúscula colada na margem
questions.answer: Com um pequeno espaço da margem e letra maiúscula
questions.hint: Olhe o começo dos parágrafos num livro.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Como se chama o pequeno espaço deixado no começo de cada parágrafo? (uma palavra)
questions.hint: Ele 'empurra' a primeira linha um pouco para dentro.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual é a linha vertical da folha onde as linhas do texto começam? (uma palavra)
questions.hint: Nos cadernos ela costuma ser vermelha ou cinza.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Quando devemos começar um novo parágrafo?
options: Quando mudamos de ideia ou de assunto
questions.answer: Quando mudamos de ideia ou de assunto
questions.hint: Cada parágrafo cuida de uma ideia.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Num texto sobre o fim de semana, qual parte ficaria melhor no primeiro parágrafo?
options: No sábado de manhã, fui com minha família à praia.
Por isso, aquele foi o melhor fim de semana do ano.
Voltamos para casa cansados no domingo à noite.
questions.answer: No sábado de manhã, fui com minha família à praia.
questions.hint: O primeiro parágrafo costuma apresentar o assunto.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual frase seria um bom final para um texto?
options: Por isso, aquele dia ficou guardado na minha memória.
Era uma vez uma menina chamada Bia.
questions.answer: Por isso, aquele dia ficou guardado na minha memória.
questions.hint: Procure a frase que fecha a história.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em geral, um texto tem três partes: introdução, desenvolvimento e ___.
questions.hint: É a parte que fecha o texto.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Em qual parte do texto contamos os acontecimentos com mais detalhes?
questions.hint: É a parte do meio.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual palavra ajuda a começar um parágrafo que conta o que aconteceu depois?
questions.hint: Ela mostra a ordem dos fatos.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Leia: 'O gato da vizinha é cinza. Ele adora dormir no sol. Ontem choveu muito na cidade e as ruas alagaram.' Qual frase deveria começar outro parágrafo?
options: O gato da vizinha é cinza.
Ontem choveu muito na cidade e as ruas alagaram.
questions.answer: Ontem choveu muito na cidade e as ruas alagaram.
questions.hint: Qual frase muda de assunto?

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Um texto escrito todo num bloco só, sem parágrafos, fica:
questions.hint: Imagine ler uma página inteira sem pausas.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Qual expressão é boa para começar o último parágrafo?
questions.hint: Ela anuncia que o texto está acabando.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Ao passar um texto a limpo, o que NÃO devemos fazer?
options: Começar o parágrafo com letra minúscula
Deixar o recuo no início do parágrafo
Usar ponto final no fim das frases
questions.answer: Começar o parágrafo com letra minúscula
questions.hint: Lembre a regra da letra inicial.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Escreva um parágrafo de 2 ou 3 frases contando o que você mais gosta de fazer no recreio. Lembre do recuo e da letra maiúscula.
questions.hint: Uma ideia só: o que você faz e por quê gosta.

questions.subject: pt
questions.q: Explique com suas palavras por que dividimos um texto em parágrafos.
questions.hint: Pense em quem vai ler o texto.

pt_leit.topic: Lendas do folclore: Iara, Boto e Mula sem cabeça

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: O que é uma lenda?
options: Uma história popular contada de geração em geração
questions.answer: Uma história popular contada de geração em geração
questions.hint: Ela passa dos avós para os netos.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual é a palavra que reúne lendas, cantigas, brincadeiras e costumes de um povo? (uma palavra)
questions.hint: Em agosto se comemora o dia dele.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Onde vive a Iara, segundo a lenda?
questions.hint: Ela é uma sereia de água doce.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Como a Iara atrai os pescadores, segundo a lenda?
questions.hint: Pense no que as sereias fazem nas histórias.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Em que região do Brasil a lenda do Boto é mais conhecida?
questions.hint: É a região do rio Amazonas.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Segundo a lenda, em que o Boto se transforma nas noites de festa?
options: num rapaz elegante vestido de branco
questions.answer: num rapaz elegante vestido de branco
questions.hint: Ele aparece nos bailes.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que o Boto usa um chapéu, segundo a lenda?
options: para esconder o furo no alto da cabeça
questions.answer: para esconder o furo no alto da cabeça
questions.hint: Os botos de verdade respiram por um orifício.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual é a característica mais marcante da Mula sem cabeça?
options: solta fogo no lugar da cabeça
questions.answer: solta fogo no lugar da cabeça
questions.hint: O nome já dá uma pista.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Segundo a lenda, em que noite a Mula sem cabeça costuma aparecer?
questions.hint: É uma noite no fim da semana.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: O que a Iara e o Boto têm em comum?
options: Os dois estão ligados aos rios
questions.answer: Os dois estão ligados aos rios
questions.hint: Pense no lugar onde cada um vive.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual diferença existe entre o Boto e a Mula sem cabeça?
options: O Boto vive na água; a Mula galopa pelos campos
Os dois só aparecem de dia
questions.answer: O Boto vive na água; a Mula galopa pelos campos
questions.hint: Compare onde cada um aparece.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual ser lendário tem os pés virados para trás e protege as florestas?
questions.hint: Ele confunde os caçadores com suas pegadas.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que as lendas costumam mudar um pouco de uma região para outra?
options: Porque são contadas oralmente e cada lugar acrescenta detalhes
Porque foram escritas por um único autor
questions.answer: Porque são contadas oralmente e cada lugar acrescenta detalhes
questions.hint: Pense em como elas passam de pessoa para pessoa.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Muitas lendas do Norte falam de rios e florestas. O que isso mostra?
options: Que as lendas refletem a natureza do lugar onde nasceram
Que no Norte não há cidades
Que as lendas são inventadas na escola
questions.answer: Que as lendas refletem a natureza do lugar onde nasceram
questions.hint: Relacione a paisagem com as histórias.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual dos seres lendários (Iara, Boto ou Mula sem cabeça) você acha mais assustador? Explique por quê.

questions.q: Caça-erros: encontre e corrija as 5 palavras escritas errado.
questions.answer: jeladeira → geladeira; tijela → tigela; larangeira → laranjeira; jelatina → gelatina; gibóia → jiboia
questions.text: No almoço de domingo, a vovó tirou da jeladeira uma tijela cheia de salada. No quintal, perto da larangeira, havia um girassol enorme. Depois da sobremesa de jelatina, ela contou uma história sobre uma gibóia que morava na floresta e era tratada como uma rainha, com toda a majestade.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Caça-erros: encontre e corrija as 5 palavras escritas errado nesta história do hospital.
questions.answer: jesso → gesso; jenjiva → gengiva; jirassol → girassol; tijela → tigela; jelatina → gelatina
questions.text: Rafa caiu da bicicleta e precisou colocar jesso no braço. No hospital, a enfermeira viu que a jenjiva dele também estava machucada. Para animar o menino, a mãe preparou berinjela assada, comprou um jirassol para a mesa e disse que ele era tratado como sua majestade. Até a vizinha trouxe uma tijela de sopa e uma jelatina.
